item.meaning: Geometric relationship where two plane figures have identical shape and identical size.
The process of placing one geometric figure directly over another to test for exact overlap.
Transformations (translation, rotation, reflection) that preserve distances and angle measures.
Matching relationship between specific vertices, sides, and angles of two figures.

item.definition: Two triangles are congruent if all corresponding sides are equal in length and all corresponding angles are equal in measure.
Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are equal.
A triangle with at least two equal sides and equal angles opposite to those sides.
A triangle with three equal sides and three interior angles each measuring 60°.

item.description: In congruence statements like ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ, the order of vertices strictly dictates matching pairs: A↔X, B↔Y, C↔Z.

item.statement: In any triangle, angles opposite to equal sides are equal in measure.

item.property_name: Sum of Angles in a Triangle
item.statement: The sum of the three interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

item.rule_text: If three sides of one triangle are equal to three sides of another triangle, the triangles are congruent.
If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and the included angle of another, the triangles are congruent.
If two angles and one side (included or non-included) of one triangle equal two angles and corresponding side of another, the triangles are congruent.
In two right-angled triangles, if the hypotenuse and one leg of one triangle equal the hypotenuse and one leg of the other, the triangles are congruent.

item.conversion_factors: Full rotation = 360°; Right angle = 90°; Straight angle = 180°

item.application: Test congruence of two plane figures by cutting out a tracing paper replica and attempting exact overlap.
